en: The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of Hārītī Mātā.
[Recorded by] Kai-fu Yi-tong-san-si, Te-jin, Shi Hong-lu-qing, Duke of Su with a fief of three thousand households,
invested with purple robes, posthumously titled司空 (Sikong) and granted the posthumous name Da-jian (Great Mirror).
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Monastery, who possesses Great and Vast Wisdom, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, the yakṣiṇī Hārītī rose from her seat within the assembly of the Buddha.
Prostrating with his five limbs touching the ground at the Buddha’s feet,
he addressed the Buddha, saying,
"I have a heart-mantra."
Just as the cintāmaṇi jewel can fulfill all wishes and aspirations,
[this teaching] is for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all sons and daughters of good family in Jambudvīpa.
I only pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion, will grant me leave;
I shall now speak it.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ nu nu ma-ri-kā-hite svāhā. If there is a woman who is unable to conceive a child, or whose pregnancy ends in miscarriage such that the lineage is severed and cannot be restored;
This is entirely due to the four great elements being unable to achieve equilibrium;
or it is because spirits and deities have created various obstacles and difficulties;
or it is because the causal conditions of past karma are unfavorable for the union of male and female.
One should take a piece of white cotton cloth, measuring either one cubit, one span, or five inches in length— of whatever size suits one’s preference—
and paint the Mother Hariti in the form of a celestial maiden, entirely golden in color.
He wears celestial garments and is adorned with a crown and necklaces;
seated upon a preaching throne, he extends his two feet downward.
On either side of the hanging feet, one should paint two children.
Standing beside the altar,
he has a child seated upon each of his two knees,
and with his left hand, he cradles another child in his embrace.
In his right hand, he holds an auspicious fruit (*bhadra-pūṭa*).
The painter should observe the eight precepts (*aṣṭāṅga-śīla*),
and no animal glue should be used in the pigments.
Once the painted image has been completed,
one should thoroughly clean a room, adorn it with ritual implements, and wipe it down;
then, prepare a square altar by smearing it with incense.
Place the image within the mandala.
Scatter various kinds of flowers upon the mandala.
Furthermore, offer sweet and succulent foods, milk gruel, curd-rice, various fruits, and *argha* water.
Burn aloeswood incense as an offering.
With the image facing west and the reciter facing east,
perform the recitation before the image three times each day.
At that time, recite separately one thousand times.
Begin on the fifth day of the waxing moon;
first, recite one hundred thousand times.
Thereafter, one should perform recitation before the image;
all that is sought will be completely fulfilled.
Furthermore, there is a method for a woman who desires to obtain a son or daughter.
After menstruation, one should bathe.
Then, taking a yellow cow whose calf is of the same color,
one should milk one *śroṇa* (one *āḍhaka*) of milk and place it in a silver vessel.
Stir the breast with the ring finger of the right hand while reciting the mantra one thousand and eighty times for empowerment;
thereafter, take it and consume it.
Within seven days, one will then conceive. Furthermore,
if one wishes to cause others to feel joy, respect, and affection,
one may offer food, drink, fruit, flowers, or incense.
Perform the empowerment one hundred and eight times.
Insert the person's name into the mantra phrases;
when given to that person, they will attain joy, love, and respect.
Furthermore, if there is someone who creates obstacles or engages in verbal disputes,
one should draw that person’s image and step upon it with the left foot.
By reciting the mantra one hundred and eighty times, one will be free from such difficulties.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause all people to rejoice,
one should take powdered ox-gall and place it in a silver vessel.
Following the previous method, stir it with the ring finger while reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times to empower it.
If one applies [this substance] to the forehead, all who see it will be filled with joy and submit in obedience.
Furthermore, another method is that if one obtains new clothing,
one should empower it before the image by reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times.
Thereafter, one will be taken up by all people, and they will likewise rejoice in,
respect, and love them. Furthermore, if there is a bad dream,
one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.
Then one will obtain the elimination of bad dreams.
Furthermore, there is another method: if it is during a lunar eclipse, take five *liang* of clarified butter and place it in a golden vessel.
Stir with a golden spoon,
ensuring that the recitation and empowerment do not become interrupted,
continuing until the month has reached its full completion.
Then, take one portion to offer to Hārītī;
eat the remainder gradually.

Thereupon, one will conceive and give birth to sons or daughters who are wise and possessed of merit. Furthermore, there is another method: take the root of *gokṣura* (Eclipta alba) to serve as a tooth-stick.
If one performs the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) one hundred and eight times and then chews [the substance] and uses it to brush the teeth, the words spoken will be pleasing to others to hear.
Whatever matters one desires from others will all be accomplished according to one's wishes. Furthermore, there is another method for those who wish to attain a long life.
Take *kṣīra* grass and tender sprouts,
dip them in ghee, honey, and curd, and perform *homa* for seven nights.
Each night, recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
If one recites [the mantra] once and casts it into the fire,
one will attain longevity. Furthermore, for those who wish to have whatever they intend to do accomplished according to their wishes,
on the fifth and twentieth days of every month:
Anoint and wipe the maṇḍala, scatter flowers,
and prepare various foods and drinks, including milk-rice, curd-rice, and other grains,
as well as fruits, arghya water, and fragrant perfumes.
Burn aloeswood and frankincense as an offering.
First, make offerings to all the Tathāgatas, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra, and all other bodhisattvas.
Thereafter, you should make offerings to me, Hārītī Mātā. Why is this?
I was originally a yakṣī.
The Tathāgata bestowed upon me the three refuges, the five precepts, and the bodhicitta-śīla-saṃvara.
Because this was in the presence of the Bodhisattvas of the ten stages,
I first made offerings to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Having made the offerings,
recite [the mantra] ten thousand times before this image;
all sought-after undertakings will be fully accomplished.
The method for the recitation of Hārītī’s mantra.
The heart-mantra for her beloved son is:
Oṃ jñe jñāne svāhā. As for the mudrā: join the palms and bend the two thumbs so that they enter into the center of the hands.
Having completed the offering by reciting the heart mantra,
release the two thumbs at the crown of the head and they shall disperse.
This same mudrā is used for both summoning and dismissal.
Using white sandalwood,
fashion the form of a youth six finger-widths in length,
complete with two hands, each holding a sweetmeat and offering it to others.
Form three topknots on the head and place it in a secluded and pure location;
recite the mantra ten thousand times.
He immediately manifested his body and asked,
"For what purpose do you call me?
She answered him according to her thoughts.
Take a piece of yellow ox meat the size of a square inch.
Perform one consecration and burn it three times each day.
After four days have passed, one will attain great mastery according to one's wishes.
Furthermore, there is another method: make pills from beef and guggulu incense.
On the eighth day of the month, recite the mantra at the three times of day, burning the aforementioned incense eighteen times.
When the tenth day has arrived,
at midnight, a great light-appearance will manifest and one will attain great supernatural power (*mahā-ṛddhi*).
Taking *agaru* incense and forming it into pills, perform one consecration (*adhitiṣṭhati*) for each pill and burn them three times daily.
At that time, by reciting [the mantra] one thousand and eight times separately for five days, one subdues all people.
Furthermore, there is a method: by consecrating each flower from a hundred kinds of grass and scattering them upon one's body, one obtains clothing and food for a thousand people.
Furthermore, there is a method: recite the mantra daily while burning *sugandha* incense for seven days, and you will see a treasury of gold beneath the earth.
Then, offer various flowers, fruits, food, and drink within the mandala as an act of worship.
In this manner, one shall obtain all manner of wealth and treasures day by day.
Furthermore, there is another method: mix *guggulu* with milk porridge;
empower each portion once and burn it for seven days.
Recite one thousand and eight times for each of the three periods of the day.
One will be able to converse with the manifested form and inquire of its intentions.
Furthermore, there is a method for when one is imprisoned.
Reciting it ten thousand times brings immediate liberation.
To cure illnesses, empower *āmra* (mango) sprouts by soaking them in milk, then burn them after empowerment;
this eliminates all diseases.
The Sūtra of Hārītī Mātṛkā
